findings.title: The declared CP0007 review bundle cannot be reconstructed from its sealed subject
findings.originalExpected: A sealed review-bundle declaration identifies immutable published content from which the declared digest and size can be reproduced exactly.
findings.originalObserved: Two valid byte-identical archives rebuilt from CP0007's final published subject had digest 07bb328a4316297d0b6bd2df986c7b5f5fb41b30c8b2fb58cd99a8d96c24c168, not the declared digest 8856ce50acebfa02528ad318247c22e6e460c224eb62774c99a35cb5cd734578.
findings.rootCause: The schema 3.3 producer collected mutable working-tree and live remote observations, and wrote its declaration before finalization and sealing changed checkpoint content. No immutable subject or declared-versus-rebuilt comparison existed, and the declaration's self-reference boundary was implicit.
implementation: Checkpoint schema 3.4.0 defines the archive over a named immutable Git content commit and tree.
The producer reads canonical bytes only from Git objects and excludes exactly REVIEW-BUNDLE-VALIDATION.json to break declaration self-reference.

Sealing clones through non-local Git transport, checks out the content commit detached, executes the subject-carried producer twice, and requires valid byte-identical archives before writing the declaration.
Checkpoint validation independently performs two transported reconstructions and compares their digest, size and entry count with the declaration.
The seal evidence chronology permits the declaration sidecar and no broader delivery change.
negativeTest: BASELINE-BUNDLE-AUDIT.json preserves the CP0007 declaration mismatch as the red control.
test_declared_digest_and_size_are_rebuilt_not_trusted mutates the declaration digest and requires refusal.
Attack T reconstructs twice through detached Git transport and rejects a stale declaration.
